answer: To resist Sybil attacks, an agent economy can tie identity validation to a cryptographic pulse of sequential delay functions, backed by collateral in an unbonding glacier. Attackers cannot parallelize these proofs, incurring the verifiable cost of dedicated hardware and locked capital per identity. While this stops the network from becoming a haven for disposable bots, a key limitation is that ongoing compute demands and illiquid deposits heavily burden lightweight, honest agents.
